The fog had been thick for three days, swallowing the horizon whole. Elias, the keeper of the lonely Sentinel Point Lighthouse, sat in his small, damp kitchen, listening to the rhythmic *thump-thump* of the foghorn. It was a sound that had become as familiar to him as his own heartbeat.

He was mending a net when he noticed something bobbing against the base of the lighthouse’s stone foundation. It wasn’t a piece of driftwood or a tangled knot of seaweed. It was a bottle, green glass, sealed with wax that had long since cracked.

Elias waded out into the shallow, freezing water, his boots squelching in the mud. He retrieved the bottle and brought it inside, placing it on the table beside his cold tea. The label was faded, but the paper inside was surprisingly intact. He carefully extracted the scroll, his hands trembling slightly—not from the cold, but from the sudden intrusion of the past
